backlog-hygiene.4c84ad7a63527d297d01ba42b3bf25b523f80074:
schemaVersion: 1
name: backlog-hygiene
description: Weekly report of stalled and untriaged tasks for human follow-up
enabled: false
schedule:
  cron: 30 7 * * 1
template:
  title: Report backlog hygiene candidates
  description: |-
    Produce one read-only backlog hygiene report for this workspace. The report
    is the task's persisted execution_summary; an empty report is a successful
    no-op. Snapshot the scan time in UTC and state the thresholds below.

    ## Safety and evidence

    - Do not change any task's status, approve, reject, dispatch, retry, resume,
      cancel, or mint work. Do not invoke status-changing task tools or workflow
      commands. Approval and disposition belong to a human. Do not edit Orbit
      state files directly. The only permitted write is this report through
      `orbit.task.update` with execution_summary; at most one comment per flagged
      task is optional and must contain no status change.
    - List each nonterminal status separately with
      `orbit tool run orbit.task.list --input '{"status":["blocked","in-progress","review","proposed","backlog","someday"],"limit":10000,"model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
      Check `truncated` and raise the limit if needed; a partial task corpus is
      not a clean scan. Inspect candidates and their dependencies with
      `orbit tool run orbit.task.show --input '{"id":"<id>","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
      Use the task's status-entry event in `history` to age blocked, in-progress,
      and review states; use `created_at` for proposed age. If history is absent,
      say which timestamp was substituted rather than implying certainty.
    - Read job runs through `orbit run history --limit <n> --json` and
      `orbit run show <run-id> --json`. Increase the history limit until it
      covers every candidate's linked `job_run_id` and the seven-day lookback;
      use the task's linked run as primary evidence. A missing run is unknown,
      not proof of failure. Do not read or edit the Orbit database.

    ## Candidate rules

    1. Blocked: status has lasted at least 7 days. Quote the latest blocking
       reason from task comments/history or description, and the linked run's
       state, completion time, and error when available. If either is absent,
       write "not recorded". Recommend the specific owner or credential check
       needed to unblock, without performing it.
    2. Orphaned: in-progress for at least 48 hours, or review for at least 7
       days, with no linked job run currently pending/running and no linked run
       started or finished in the last 48 hours. A missing linked run qualifies
       only after the status-age threshold. Check the linked run directly before
       labeling it orphaned; report its last known outcome or "no linked run".
       Recommend checking the worker or review owner before any re-dispatch.
    3. Proposed: created at least 14 days ago and still proposed. Group rows
       as likely duplicate, possibly already landed, or needs triage. Compare
       title/scope with open and closed tasks using
       `orbit tool run orbit.search --input '{"query":"<one distinctive term>","kind":"task","all":true,"model":"<agent-family>"}'`
       and inspect plausible matches. Check `git log --all --oneline --grep=<task-id>`
       for each candidate. A log match is a lead, not proof that the exact work
       landed; inspect the commit before recommending closure. Never reject a
       task based on a title match alone.
    4. Dependency-unblocked but idle: backlog or someday tasks with at least
       one dependency, every dependency now done or rejected, and no status
       transition for at least 7 days after the last dependency entered its
       terminal status. Read each dependency's status and history; a rejected
       dependency may invalidate the task, so recommend reassessment rather
       than automatic pickup. If the latest terminal time is unavailable,
       report the uncertainty and do not claim the age threshold is met.

    ## Output

    Persist one execution_summary with scan time, thresholds, task and run
    coverage, and a Markdown table for each category. Every flagged row needs
    task id, age in the relevant status (or age since dependency clearance),
    concise evidence, and a recommended human action. Proposed rows also name
    their group and any duplicate task or candidate commit. A task may appear
    in more than one category; cross-reference rather than hiding it. Record
    counts and uncertainty explicitly. If no rows qualify, write the zero
    counts and "No action needed"; do not create filler work.
  acceptance_criteria:
  - The execution summary states scan time, thresholds, coverage, and a table for each of the four categories, with id, age, evidence, and recommended action for every flagged task.
  - Blocked rows include reason and linked run outcome; orphaned rows distinguish live, recent, missing, and terminal run evidence; proposed rows include duplicate and git-log checks; dependency rows verify every dependency's terminal status.
  - No task status was changed, no task was approved or rejected, and no work was dispatched; an empty scan is a successful no-op.
  task_type: chore
  tags:
  - backlog-hygiene
  - no-diff-expected
  required_tools:
  - orbit.task.list
  - orbit.task.show
  - orbit.search
  priority: medium
  complexity: medium
  crew: system
  status: backlog
dedupe: skip_if_open
created_by: system
created_at: 2026-09-24T00:00:00Z
updated_by: system
updated_at: 2026-09-24T00:00:00Z

code-review.076c722f6ec06e51d4b1f9256851b82851e2bb6c:
schemaVersion: 1
name: code-review
description: Post-merge code review of changes merged since the last completed sweep
enabled: false
schedule:
  cron: 40 */6 * * *
template:
  title: Review recently merged changes
  description: |-
    Review the code merged into this workspace since the last completed sweep.
    The durable output is filed Orbit tasks for every confirmed finding plus the
    recorded review cursor; the execution summary is the audit trail. Narrative-only
    output does not count as delivery.

    ## Rules and command surfaces

    - Use the registered Orbit tool surface. Find the newest current-name sweep with
      `orbit tool run orbit.task.list --input '{"status":["done"],"type":"chore","tag":["code-review","no-diff-expected"],"limit":1,"model":"<agent-family>"}'`
      and the newest legacy-name sweep with
      `orbit tool run orbit.task.list --input '{"status":["done"],"type":"chore","tag":["code-review-sweep","no-diff-expected"],"limit":1,"model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
      Both tag filters use AND semantics. Compare the first result from each
      newest-first list by `created_at`, with the lexicographically smaller task ID
      winning an equal timestamp, and read the selected sweep's cursor with
      `orbit tool run orbit.task.show --input '{"id":"<id>","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
      A finding is a `bug` tagged only `code-review`, so it is never a sweep
      candidate even when it completed after the selected sweep.
      Search existing coverage with
      `orbit tool run orbit.search --input '{"query":"<distinctive symptom, symbol, or file terms>","kind":"task","all":true,"model":"<agent-family>"}'`
      and list open review work with
      `orbit tool run orbit.task.list --input '{"status":["backlog","in-progress","proposed","blocked"],"tag":"code-review","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
      File a finding with
      `orbit tool run orbit.task.add --input '{"title":"<title>","description":"<markdown>","acceptance_criteria":["<observable outcome>"],"complexity":"medium","tags":["code-review"],"priority":"<low|medium|high|critical>","type":"bug","relations":[{"type":"regression_from","target":"<culprit task ID>"}],"workspace":"<current workspace path>","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
      Omit `relations` only when no task in the window can be held responsible.
      Do not use direct lifecycle CLI subcommands; they skip agent provenance.
    - Fail open. A window with no confirmed findings is a successful no-op. Do not
      invent work to justify the run.

    ## Determine the review window

    Run both completed-sweep queries above and select the newer result using the
    stated ordering. Read the last-reviewed commit recorded in that sweep's
    execution summary, then review the commits from that point to the current HEAD
    of the workspace's integration branch. Never use a `code-review`-only finding
    as a cursor, and never treat a selected sweep's missing cursor as a first run.
    If neither sweep query returns a result, record the current HEAD as the baseline
    and stop — only that case seeds the cursor.

    ## Review the window

    Read the diffs white-box: correctness, concurrency and error handling, and
    conformance to the repository's documented standards (agent guide, contributing
    guide, lint configuration). Review the window as a whole — interactions between
    separately merged changes are findings per-change review cannot see.

    ## Attribute each finding to the task that introduced it

    Every finding is a regression from a change that landed in the window, so
    name the task that caused it. Find the commit that introduced the defect
    (`git log -L` or `git blame` on the offending lines, restricted to the
    reviewed range) and read the task ID from that commit: squash-merge subjects
    carry it as `[<task-id>]`, and the delivery's pull request references it
    otherwise. Confirm with `orbit.task.show` that the task exists and that its
    change is the one at fault — blame the commit that introduced the defect, not
    a later commit that merely touched the same file. When the defect spans
    several tasks' changes, blame the one whose change made the code wrong.
    When the culprit commit carries no task ID, or the defect predates the
    window and was only exposed by it, say so in the finding and file it without
    the relation rather than blaming a bystander.

    ## File confirmed findings

    Verify every finding against the live code before filing — a diff that looks
    wrong but is guarded elsewhere is not a finding. Search open Orbit tasks tagged
    `code-review` before filing; skip duplicates and nitpicks. File each confirmed
    finding as its own Orbit task with file:line evidence, a severity-appropriate
    priority, the `code-review` tag, and a `regression_from` relation targeting
    the task identified above. The finding's description names the culprit task
    and the commit that introduced the defect.

    ## Findings that narrow a shared invariant

    When a finding is a repair that narrows a shared invariant — what the host
    will create, what URLs are accepted, what counts as first-party, or any
    other predicate with more than one caller — search for every caller and
    fixture of that predicate and name them in the filed task's description;
    its acceptance criteria must require the same change to update all of
    them together, not just the call site that produced the observed symptom.

    A pull request that is green only against its own base is not evidence
    the merged tree is green. When the finding shares an invariant with other
    in-flight work, the filed task's acceptance criteria must require
    comparing the per-commit suite on the integration branch against its
    parent commit, not just a green check on the PR's own base.

    ## Record the cursor

    Always record the reviewed range and the new last-reviewed commit in the
    persisted execution summary — the next sweep's window starts there. Record
    the same commit as this task's machine-readable cursor artifact, which the
    scheduler reads to decide whether the next tick has anything to review:
    write `{"schema_version":1,"ref":"<integration branch>","cursor":"<full 40-character commit SHA>"}`
    to a gitignored scratch file inside the checkout (for example
    `target/sweep-cursor.json`) and attach it with
    `orbit tool run orbit.task.artifact.put --input '{"id":"<this task ID>","source_path":"target/sweep-cursor.json","path":"sweep-cursor.json","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
    Write it on every completed sweep, including an empty window: the commit it
    names is the one this sweep examined through, and a completed sweep without
    it leaves the next tick no cursor to compare the branch tip against.
  acceptance_criteria:
  - The review window was derived from the previous sweep's recorded cursor, or the current HEAD was seeded as the baseline on the first run.
  - Every filed finding was verified against live code, is non-duplicate, and carries file:line evidence with a severity-appropriate priority and the `code-review` tag.
  - Every filed finding carries a `regression_from` relation targeting the task whose landed commit introduced the defect, or its description states why no task in the window can be held responsible.
  - The reviewed range and the new last-reviewed commit are recorded in the persisted execution summary.
  - The new last-reviewed commit is attached as this task's `sweep-cursor.json` artifact (`schema_version` 1, the integration branch, and the full commit SHA).
  - A window with no confirmed findings succeeds as a no-op.
  task_type: chore
  tags:
  - code-review
  - no-diff-expected
  priority: medium
  complexity: hard
  # The portable system lane is seeded per machine and compatibility-aliased
  # for configs written before that crew existed.
  crew: system
  status: backlog
dedupe: skip_if_open
skip_if_unchanged:
  ref: __ORBIT_BASE_BRANCH__
  cursor:
    tags:
    - code-review
    - no-diff-expected
    legacy_tags:
    - code-review-sweep
    - no-diff-expected
created_by: system
created_at: 2026-08-23T00:00:00Z
updated_by: system
updated_at: 2026-08-23T00:00:00Z

schemaVersion: 1
name: code-review
description: Post-merge code review of changes merged since the last completed sweep
enabled: false
schedule:
  cron: 40 */6 * * *
template:
  title: Review recently merged changes
  description: |-
    Review the code merged into this workspace since the last completed sweep.
    The durable output is filed Orbit tasks for every confirmed finding plus the
    recorded review cursor; the execution summary is the audit trail. Narrative-only
    output does not count as delivery.

    ## Rules and command surfaces

    - Use the registered Orbit tool surface. Find the newest current-name sweep with
      `orbit tool run orbit.task.list --input '{"status":["done"],"type":"chore","tag":["code-review","no-diff-expected","auto-task:code-review"],"limit":1,"model":"<agent-family>"}'`
      and the newest legacy-name sweep with
      `orbit tool run orbit.task.list --input '{"status":["done"],"type":"chore","tag":["code-review-sweep","no-diff-expected"],"limit":1,"model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
      Both tag filters use AND semantics. Compare the first result from each
      newest-first list by `created_at`, with the lexicographically smaller task ID
      winning an equal timestamp, and read the selected sweep's cursor with
      `orbit tool run orbit.task.show --input '{"id":"<id>","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
      A finding is a `bug` tagged only `code-review`, so it is never a sweep
      candidate even when it completed after the selected sweep. The
      `auto-task:code-review` provenance tag is carried only by tasks minted from
      this definition, so a hand-filed or full-review chore that shares the
      other tags never displaces a real sweep's cursor.
      Search existing coverage with
      `orbit tool run orbit.search --input '{"query":"<distinctive symptom, symbol, or file terms>","kind":"task","all":true,"model":"<agent-family>"}'`
      and list open review work with
      `orbit tool run orbit.task.list --input '{"status":["backlog","in-progress","proposed","blocked"],"tag":"code-review","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
      File a finding with
      `orbit tool run orbit.task.add --input '{"title":"<title>","description":"<markdown>","acceptance_criteria":["<observable outcome>"],"complexity":"medium","tags":["code-review"],"context_files":["file:<evidence source path>","file:<matching test path>"],"priority":"<low|medium|high|critical>","type":"bug","relations":[{"type":"spawned_from","target":"<this task ID>"},{"type":"regression_from","target":"<culprit task ID>"}],"workspace":"<current workspace path>","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
      Omit the `regression_from` relation only when no task in the window can be
      held responsible. Derive canonical `file:` selectors from every evidenced
      source path, removing the line suffix, and add the matching
      regression-test location. Use existing paths where possible; for a test file
      that must be created, set `allow_missing_context: true` and identify that
      intended path. Never file a finding without context selectors.
      Do not use direct lifecycle CLI subcommands; they skip agent provenance.
    - Fail open. A window with no confirmed findings is a successful no-op. Do not
      invent work to justify the run.

    ## Determine the review window

    Run both completed-sweep queries above and select the newer result using the
    stated ordering. Read the last-reviewed commit recorded in that sweep's
    execution summary, then review the commits from that point to the current HEAD
    of the workspace's integration branch. Never use a `code-review`-only finding
    as a cursor, and never treat a selected sweep's missing cursor as a first run.
    If neither sweep query returns a result, record the current HEAD as the baseline
    and stop — only that case seeds the cursor.

    ## Review the window

    Read the diffs white-box: correctness, concurrency and error handling, and
    conformance to the repository's documented standards (agent guide, contributing
    guide, lint configuration). Review the window as a whole — interactions between
    separately merged changes are findings per-change review cannot see.

    ## Attribute each finding to the task that introduced it

    Every finding is a regression from a change that landed in the window, so
    name the task that caused it. Find the commit that introduced the defect
    (`git log -L` or `git blame` on the offending lines, restricted to the
    reviewed range) and read the task ID from that commit: squash-merge subjects
    carry it as `[<task-id>]`, and the delivery's pull request references it
    otherwise. Confirm with `orbit.task.show` that the task exists and that its
    change is the one at fault — blame the commit that introduced the defect, not
    a later commit that merely touched the same file. When the defect spans
    several tasks' changes, blame the one whose change made the code wrong.
    When the culprit commit carries no task ID, or the defect predates the
    window and was only exposed by it, say so in the finding and file it without
    the relation rather than blaming a bystander.

    ## File confirmed findings

    Verify every finding against the live code before filing — a diff that looks
    wrong but is guarded elsewhere is not a finding. Search open Orbit tasks tagged
    `code-review` before filing; skip duplicates and nitpicks. File each confirmed
    finding as its own Orbit task with file:line evidence, a severity-appropriate
    priority, the `code-review` tag, and a `regression_from` relation targeting
    the task identified above. The finding's description names the culprit task
    and the commit that introduced the defect.

    ## Findings that narrow a shared invariant

    When a finding is a repair that narrows a shared invariant — what the host
    will create, what URLs are accepted, what counts as first-party, or any
    other predicate with more than one caller — search for every caller and
    fixture of that predicate and name them in the filed task's description;
    its acceptance criteria must require the same change to update all of
    them together, not just the call site that produced the observed symptom.

    A pull request that is green only against its own base is not evidence
    the merged tree is green. When the finding shares an invariant with other
    in-flight work, the filed task's acceptance criteria must require
    comparing the per-commit suite on the integration branch against its
    parent commit, not just a green check on the PR's own base.

    ## Record the cursor

    Always record the reviewed range and the new last-reviewed commit in the
    persisted execution summary — the next sweep's window starts there. Record
    the same commit as this task's machine-readable cursor artifact, which the
    scheduler reads to decide whether the next tick has anything to review:
    write `{"schema_version":1,"ref":"<integration branch>","cursor":"<full 40-character commit SHA>"}`
    to a gitignored scratch file inside the checkout (for example
    `.orbit/tmp/sweep-cursor.json`) and attach it with
    `orbit tool run orbit.task.artifact.put --input '{"id":"<this task ID>","source_path":".orbit/tmp/sweep-cursor.json","path":"sweep-cursor.json","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
    `orbit tool show <tool.name>` prints the tool's schema.
    Write it on every completed sweep, including an empty window: the commit it
    names is the one this sweep examined through, and a completed sweep without
    it leaves the next tick no cursor to compare the branch tip against.
  acceptance_criteria:
  - The review window was derived from the previous sweep's recorded cursor, or the current HEAD was seeded as the baseline on the first run.
  - Every filed finding was verified against live code, is non-duplicate, and carries file:line evidence with a severity-appropriate priority and the `code-review` tag.
  - Every filed finding carries a `regression_from` relation targeting the task whose landed commit introduced the defect, or its description states why no task in the window can be held responsible.
  - The reviewed range and the new last-reviewed commit are recorded in the persisted execution summary.
  - The new last-reviewed commit is attached as this task's `sweep-cursor.json` artifact (`schema_version` 1, the integration branch, and the full commit SHA).
  - A window with no confirmed findings succeeds as a no-op.
  task_type: chore
  tags:
  - code-review
  - no-diff-expected
  required_tools:
  - orbit.search
  - orbit.task.add
  - orbit.task.list
  - orbit.task.show
  priority: medium
  complexity: hard
  # The portable system lane is seeded per machine and compatibility-aliased
  # for configs written before that crew existed.
  crew: system
  status: backlog
dedupe: skip_if_open

    tags:
    - code-review
    - no-diff-expected
    - auto-task:code-review
    legacy_tags:
    - code-review-sweep
    - no-diff-expected

schemaVersion: 1
name: code-review
description: Post-merge code review of changes merged since the last completed sweep
enabled: false
schedule:
  cron: 40 */6 * * *
template:
  title: Review recently merged changes
  description: |-
    Review the code merged into this workspace since the last completed sweep.
    The durable output is filed Orbit tasks for every confirmed finding plus the
    recorded review cursor; the execution summary is the audit trail. Narrative-only
    output does not count as delivery.

    ## Rules and command surfaces

    - Use the registered Orbit tool surface. Find the newest current-name sweep with
      `orbit tool run orbit.task.list --input '{"status":["done"],"type":"chore","tag":["code-review","no-diff-expected"],"limit":1,"model":"<agent-family>"}'`
      and the newest legacy-name sweep with
      `orbit tool run orbit.task.list --input '{"status":["done"],"type":"chore","tag":["code-review-sweep","no-diff-expected"],"limit":1,"model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
      Both tag filters use AND semantics. Compare the first result from each
      newest-first list by `created_at`, with the lexicographically smaller task ID
      winning an equal timestamp, and read the selected sweep's cursor with
      `orbit tool run orbit.task.show --input '{"id":"<id>","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
      A finding is a `bug` tagged only `code-review`, so it is never a sweep
      candidate even when it completed after the selected sweep.
      Search existing coverage with
      `orbit tool run orbit.search --input '{"query":"<distinctive symptom, symbol, or file terms>","kind":"task","all":true,"model":"<agent-family>"}'`
      and list open review work with
      `orbit tool run orbit.task.list --input '{"status":["backlog","in-progress","proposed","blocked"],"tag":"code-review","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
      File a finding with
      `orbit tool run orbit.task.add --input '{"title":"<title>","description":"<markdown>","acceptance_criteria":["<observable outcome>"],"complexity":"medium","tags":["code-review"],"priority":"<low|medium|high|critical>","type":"bug","relations":[{"type":"regression_from","target":"<culprit task ID>"}],"workspace":"<current workspace path>","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
      Omit `relations` only when no task in the window can be held responsible.
      Do not use direct lifecycle CLI subcommands; they skip agent provenance.
    - Fail open. A window with no confirmed findings is a successful no-op. Do not
      invent work to justify the run.

    ## Determine the review window

    Run both completed-sweep queries above and select the newer result using the
    stated ordering. Read the last-reviewed commit recorded in that sweep's
    execution summary, then review the commits from that point to the current HEAD
    of the workspace's integration branch. Never use a `code-review`-only finding
    as a cursor, and never treat a selected sweep's missing cursor as a first run.
    If neither sweep query returns a result, record the current HEAD as the baseline
    and stop — only that case seeds the cursor.

    ## Review the window

    Read the diffs white-box: correctness, concurrency and error handling, and
    conformance to the repository's documented standards (agent guide, contributing
    guide, lint configuration). Review the window as a whole — interactions between
    separately merged changes are findings per-change review cannot see.

    ## Attribute each finding to the task that introduced it

    Every finding is a regression from a change that landed in the window, so
    name the task that caused it. Find the commit that introduced the defect
    (`git log -L` or `git blame` on the offending lines, restricted to the
    reviewed range) and read the task ID from that commit: squash-merge subjects
    carry it as `[<task-id>]`, and the delivery's pull request references it
    otherwise. Confirm with `orbit.task.show` that the task exists and that its
    change is the one at fault — blame the commit that introduced the defect, not
    a later commit that merely touched the same file. When the defect spans
    several tasks' changes, blame the one whose change made the code wrong.
    When the culprit commit carries no task ID, or the defect predates the
    window and was only exposed by it, say so in the finding and file it without
    the relation rather than blaming a bystander.

    ## File confirmed findings

    Verify every finding against the live code before filing — a diff that looks
    wrong but is guarded elsewhere is not a finding. Search open Orbit tasks tagged
    `code-review` before filing; skip duplicates and nitpicks. File each confirmed
    finding as its own Orbit task with file:line evidence, a severity-appropriate
    priority, the `code-review` tag, and a `regression_from` relation targeting
    the task identified above. The finding's description names the culprit task
    and the commit that introduced the defect.

    ## Record the cursor

    Always record the reviewed range and the new last-reviewed commit in the
    persisted execution summary — the next sweep's window starts there. Record
    the same commit as this task's machine-readable cursor artifact, which the
    scheduler reads to decide whether the next tick has anything to review:
    write `{"schema_version":1,"ref":"<integration branch>","cursor":"<full 40-character commit SHA>"}`
    to a gitignored scratch file inside the checkout (for example
    `target/sweep-cursor.json`) and attach it with
    `orbit tool run orbit.task.artifact.put --input '{"id":"<this task ID>","source_path":"target/sweep-cursor.json","path":"sweep-cursor.json","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
    Write it on every completed sweep, including an empty window: the commit it
    names is the one this sweep examined through, and a completed sweep without
    it leaves the next tick no cursor to compare the branch tip against.
  acceptance_criteria:
  - The review window was derived from the previous sweep's recorded cursor, or the current HEAD was seeded as the baseline on the first run.
  - Every filed finding was verified against live code, is non-duplicate, and carries file:line evidence with a severity-appropriate priority and the `code-review` tag.
  - Every filed finding carries a `regression_from` relation targeting the task whose landed commit introduced the defect, or its description states why no task in the window can be held responsible.
  - The reviewed range and the new last-reviewed commit are recorded in the persisted execution summary.
  - The new last-reviewed commit is attached as this task's `sweep-cursor.json` artifact (`schema_version` 1, the integration branch, and the full commit SHA).
  - A window with no confirmed findings succeeds as a no-op.
  task_type: chore
  tags:
  - code-review
  - no-diff-expected
  priority: medium
  complexity: medium

  # for configs written before that crew existed.
  crew: system
  status: backlog

    captured commit, including unattributed neighbors. Findings may remain open.

    finding text.

    and attach automation-coverage.json through orbit.task.artifact.put in this
    task's assigned executor run. Supply actual checks (subject, method,
    observation); set examination_complete only after all obligations are examined.

doc-duties.7983d6ab36a7ca9e7e5ae24a03ea513446f6ce5a:
schemaVersion: 1
name: doc-duties
description: Daily rolling verification of workspace documentation against current behavior
enabled: false
schedule:
  cron: 30 6 * * *
template:
  title: Validate the oldest workspace documentation
  description: |
    Validate a small batch of documentation against the current repository.
    Correct factual drift and broken links or Markdown. A batch whose claims
    are already accurate is a successful no-diff run.

    ## Select a batch

    1. List tracked Markdown files under `docs/` and tracked top-level
       `README*` or `CONTRIBUTING*` documents with `git ls-files`. Exclude vendored
       dependencies, generated trees and indexes, archives, and files the
       repository identifies as generated or historical records. Use repository
       guidance for any additional documentation scope; do not edit unrelated
       files. Keep the paths relative to the repository root.
    2. For each candidate, read a valid `last_validated: YYYY-MM-DD` value in
       existing YAML frontmatter when present. Otherwise obtain its last-touched
       date with `git log -1 --format=%cI -- <path>`. Use the date part of that
       timestamp as the initial validation age. Report invalid frontmatter
       values and missing git history rather than treating them as real dates.
    3. If previous completed doc-duties execution summaries record a later
       validation date for a candidate without `last_validated`, use the latest
       recorded date as its age. This lets a no-frontmatter repository rotate
       after a clean no-diff batch. Otherwise retain the git-derived date.
    4. Sort candidates by validation age, oldest first, breaking ties by
       relative path. Take at most six. If no candidates have a usable age,
       explain why in the execution summary and finish without a diff.

    ## Validate and record

    For each selected document, check factual claims against current source,
    commands, configuration, and related documentation. Correct verified drift,
    genuine spelling errors, and broken Markdown or relative links. Preserve
    the author's style and avoid unrelated rewrites. If a claim cannot be
    checked, leave it unchanged and record the limit.

    Update `last_validated` to today's date only when that key already exists
    and the document was actually verified. Never add YAML frontmatter or a
    `last_validated` key to a document that lacks it. Record every verified
    document, including unchanged ones, in this task's durable
    `execution_summary` with the validation date and supporting checks.

    The execution summary must list the selected paths in order, each path's
    ordering date and source (frontmatter, git, or prior summary), changes and
    verification evidence, and any skipped document or unverified claim. State
    explicitly when the batch was clean. Do not manufacture an edit to mark a
    clean run complete.
  acceptance_criteria:
  - Up to six least-recently-validated tracked documents were selected by date and stable path order, using git last-touched dates where no validation metadata or prior summary exists.
  - Each selected document was checked against current evidence; verified drift was corrected, while unverifiable claims were left unchanged and reported.
  - No frontmatter or last_validated key was added to a document that lacked it; existing last_validated keys were updated only after verification.
  - The durable execution summary records selected paths, ordering evidence, checks, changes, and skipped claims, including clean no-diff batches.
  task_type: chore
  tags:
  - doc-duties
  - docs
  - no-diff-expected
  priority: medium
  complexity: low
  crew: system
  status: backlog

doc-duties.89e66f6ff7e568dc1ddfb2921e38460fe167e2b8:
schemaVersion: 1
name: doc-duties
description: Daily rolling verification of workspace documentation against current behavior
enabled: false
schedule:
  cron: 30 6 * * *
template:
  title: Validate the oldest workspace documentation
  description: |
    Validate a small batch of documentation against the current repository.
    Correct factual drift and broken links or Markdown. A batch whose claims
    are already accurate is a successful no-diff run with validated no-diff
    evidence.

    ## Select a batch

    1. List tracked Markdown files under `docs/` and tracked top-level
       `README*` or `CONTRIBUTING*` documents with `git ls-files`. Exclude vendored
       dependencies, generated trees and indexes, archives, and files the
       repository identifies as generated or historical records. Use repository
       guidance for any additional documentation scope; do not edit unrelated
       files. Keep the paths relative to the repository root.
    2. Read the prior ledgers. List the newest completed instances with
       `orbit tool run orbit.task.list --input '{"status":["done"],"type":"chore","tag":["doc-duties"],"limit":60,"fields":["id"],"model":"<agent-family>"}'`
       and read each one's ledger with
       `orbit tool run orbit.task.artifact.get --input '{"id":"<id>","path":"doc-duties-ledger.json","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
       Skip a task with no ledger (a run from before ledgers existed) and ignore
       its prose summary; never order by execution-summary text. For each path
       keep every row, newest `attempted_on` first (ties: the newer task).
    3. Give each candidate an ordering date, oldest first. Precedence: the
       latest ledger `attempted_on` for that path (source `ledger`); else a
       valid `last_validated: YYYY-MM-DD` in existing YAML frontmatter (source
       `frontmatter`); else the date part of `git log -1 --format=%cI -- <path>`
       (source `git`). A candidate falls back to frontmatter or git only when
       no ledger row names it. Report invalid frontmatter values and missing git
       history rather than treating them as real dates. If no ledger could be
       read at all (no completed instance, or the artifact tools failed), say so
       explicitly in the execution summary and the ledger `notes`; do not fall
       back silently.
    4. Escalate repeat skips. A candidate whose two most recent ledger rows
       both have outcome `skipped` or `partial` is not selected. List it in the
       execution summary as needing its own task (for example section-by-section
       validation of an oversized document) with both reasons. Optionally file
       that task: first search `orbit tool run orbit.search --input '{"query":"<the path>","kind":"task","all":true,"model":"<agent-family>"}'`
       and skip the path when an open task already names it, then
       `orbit tool run orbit.task.add --input '{"title":"Validate <path> section by section","description":"<why it was skipped, with the ledger reasons>","acceptance_criteria":["<observable outcome>"],"complexity":"medium","type":"chore","tags":["docs","doc-duties-escalation"],"context_files":["file:<path>"],"relations":[{"type":"spawned_from","target":"<this task ID>"}],"priority":"low","workspace":"<current workspace path>","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
       A later `clean` or `fixed` row for the path ends the escalation.
    5. Sort the remaining candidates by ordering date, oldest first, breaking
       ties by relative path. Take at most six. If no candidates have a usable
       date, explain why in the execution summary and finish without a diff.

    ## Validate and record

    For each selected document, check factual claims against current source,
    commands, configuration, and related documentation. Correct verified drift,
    genuine spelling errors, and broken Markdown or relative links. Preserve
    the author's style and avoid unrelated rewrites. If a claim cannot be
    checked, leave it unchanged and record the limit. Give every selected
    document exactly one outcome:

    - `clean`: fully verified, no change needed.
    - `fixed`: fully verified, and drift was corrected.
    - `partial`: some claims verified, others left unchecked.
    - `skipped`: not verified (for example too large for this run), with a reason.

    Update `last_validated` to today's date only when that key already exists
    and the outcome is `clean` or `fixed`. Never add YAML frontmatter or a
    `last_validated` key to a document that lacks it, and leave it alone on
    `partial` and `skipped`.

    ## Attach the ledger

    Write `.orbit/tmp/doc-duties-ledger.json` and attach it with
    `orbit tool run orbit.task.artifact.put --input '{"id":"<this task ID>","source_path":".orbit/tmp/doc-duties-ledger.json","path":"doc-duties-ledger.json","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
    Its shape is `{"schema_version":1,"run_date":"YYYY-MM-DD","head":"<full HEAD commit SHA>","notes":"<optional, for example that no prior ledger was readable>","documents":[{"path":"<repo-relative path>","attempted_on":"YYYY-MM-DD","outcome":"clean|fixed|partial|skipped","reason":"<required unless clean or fixed>","ordering_date":"YYYY-MM-DD","ordering_source":"ledger|frontmatter|git"}]}`.
    Include one row per selected document, in selection order, and attach the
    ledger even when every document was skipped. `attempted_on` is today's date
    for every selected document regardless of outcome: it is what moves a
    skipped document to the back of the queue. Documents held back by the
    repeat-skip rule are not selected and get no row.

    The execution summary describes the batch for humans: the selected paths in
    order, each path's ordering date and source, outcome, changes and
    verification evidence, any unverified claim, any document held back for a
    dedicated task, and whether prior ledgers were readable. State explicitly
    when the batch was clean. Do not manufacture an edit to mark a clean run
    complete; when no document required changes, follow the workspace's
    validated no-diff evidence requirements (attach `no-diff.json` and captured
    validation logs).
  acceptance_criteria:
  - Up to six candidates were selected oldest first by latest ledger attempt date, then `last_validated` frontmatter, then git last-touched date, with ties broken by path; a missing ledger is stated explicitly.
  - Every selected document has an outcome of `clean`, `fixed`, `partial` or `skipped`, and a `skipped` or `partial` document gives a reason.
  - A document whose two most recent ledger outcomes are skipped or partial was not selected and is reported as needing a dedicated task.
  - No frontmatter or last_validated key was added to a document that lacked it; existing last_validated keys were updated only for `clean` or `fixed` documents.
  - A versioned `doc-duties-ledger.json` artifact records one row per selected document, and the execution summary records the batch, checks, changes, and unverified claims, including clean no-diff batches with validated no-diff evidence.
  task_type: chore
  tags:
  - doc-duties
  - docs
  required_tools:
  - orbit.search
  - orbit.task.add
  - orbit.task.artifact.get
  - orbit.task.artifact.put
  - orbit.task.list
  # A batch may edit docs/ and root or workspace-specific documentation.
  # Reserve the workspace until the batch's concrete paths are known.
  context_files:
  - 'dir:.'
  priority: medium
  complexity: low
  crew: system
  status: backlog

updated_by: system

friction-curation.00dec0d9028cb006d516ed3aba36f050c8573cc4:
schemaVersion: 1
name: friction-curation
description: Daily evidence-first deduplication, verification, resolution, and task filing for open friction records
enabled: false
schedule:
  cron: 15 7 * * *
template:
  title: Curate open friction records
  description: |-
    Curate the complete open-friction corpus in this workspace. The durable output is friction status changes and fix tasks; the execution summary is only an audit trail.

    ## Rules and command surfaces

    - Never hand-edit friction records on disk. Agents must use the registered Orbit tool surface so status and body changes go through the store: `orbit tool run orbit.friction.update --input '{"id":"<id>","body":"<replacement markdown>"}'` to edit a body, and `orbit tool run orbit.friction.update --input '{"id":"<id>","status":"resolved"}'` to resolve one. `orbit.friction.resolve` is an operator-only CLI/dashboard tool (`orbit friction resolve <id>`) that this routine cannot call; the `update` form above stamps the same resolution metadata.

schemaVersion: 1
name: friction-curation
description: Daily evidence-first deduplication, verification, resolution, and task filing for open friction records
enabled: false
schedule:
  cron: 15 7 * * *
template:
  title: Curate open friction records
  description: |-
    Curate the complete open-friction corpus in this workspace. The durable output is friction status changes and fix tasks; the execution summary is only an audit trail.

    ## Rules and command surfaces

    - Never hand-edit friction records on disk. Agents must use the registered Orbit tool surface so status and body changes go through the store: `orbit tool run orbit.friction.update --input '{"id":"<id>","body":"<replacement markdown>"}'` and `orbit tool run orbit.friction.resolve --input '{"id":"<id>"}'`, so resolution metadata is stamped by the store.
    - Frictions are a first-class `orbit search --kind friction` corpus (lexical only; hybrid remains task/doc). Snapshot the full open set with `orbit tool run orbit.friction.list --input '{"status":"open","limit":500,"offset":0,"model":"<agent-family>"}'`; keep paging until a page is shorter than the limit. Use `orbit search '<term>' --kind friction --all --json`, or `q` in the `orbit.friction.list` JSON input with `status: "open"`, to retrieve likely matches when grouping candidates. `--q` / lexical search match one case-insensitive substring: pass a single distinctive token (`EnvGuard`), never a multi-word phrase. A 0-hit whitespace-containing query is a substring miss, not proof the group is empty — retry each token on its own and read any `notes` on the empty result.
    - Search task coverage with `orbit search '<one distinctive symptom or component token>' --kind task --all --json`, then inspect plausible matches with `orbit task show <id> --json`. Do not treat a 0-hit multi-word task search as "no existing task"; retry single distinctive terms and read `notes` before certifying coverage.
    - Treat rejected tasks as historical coverage for deduplication and audit mapping, even though they are not active coverage. For every plausible rejected task, inspect the latest rejection rationale from `orbit task show <id> --json` (including its newest history/comment evidence) before deciding the friction's disposition; do not infer meaning from the status alone.
    - Before filing any fix task, read the installed `orbit` skill's task-authoring reference (`references/task-authoring.md`) completely. Follow it as the authority for general task shape, quality, provenance, and lifecycle rules. Do not duplicate that workflow here. Keep these friction-specific requirements: use the current workspace path; include evidence/reproduction and canonical modification-target `context_files`; add the `friction-curation` tag; and add exactly one `{"type":"resolves","target":"<canonical-friction-id>"}` relation for the canonical friction.
    - After every task creation, immediately read it back with `orbit.task.show <task-id> --json` (or the equivalent `orbit.task.show` tool) and verify that its relations contain exactly one `{"type":"resolves","target":"<canonical-friction-id>"}` edge. A task with a missing or incorrect edge does not count as coverage: repair its relations through `orbit.task.update` before continuing, then read it back again and verify the repaired edge. Filing a task does not itself fix the friction: leave that friction open. The relation resolves it only when the task reaches `done`.
    - Classify every rejected covering task after inspecting its latest rationale. A **terminal rejection** (intentional behavior, accepted ADR or policy decision, duplicate, obsolete report, or explicit won't-fix) can support closure only after appending a CLI/store resolution note that names the rejected task and cites the decision evidence, then resolving the friction through `orbit tool run orbit.friction.resolve --input '{"id":"<id>"}'`. An **administrative rejection** (wrong workspace, malformed or mixed scope, stale evidence, or re-homing/re-authoring required) does not fix the friction: keep it open, record the `<friction-id> -> <rejected-task-id>` mapping and the required next action, and never describe it as fixed. When the current workspace owns the issue, file at most one correctly scoped active replacement; otherwise report the re-home need without creating a wrong-lane task.
    - If a proposed fix task widens a fail-closed guard, its description and acceptance criteria must enumerate the neighboring rejection guarantees that must remain rejected (wrong workspace, malformed or mixed scope, stale evidence, re-homing/re-authoring required, and any other adjacent invalid case found during inspection) and require validation evidence for each preserved rejection. A positive reproduction alone is insufficient.
    - Fail open. Zero open frictions or a fully current corpus is a successful no-op. When evidence is genuinely ambiguous, leave the friction open and report what remains unknown.

    ## Pass

    1. Snapshot every open friction using the paginated list command above.
    2. Dedupe by underlying issue, not wording, across active, done, and rejected task history. For each group, retain the earliest well-evidenced record as canonical unless a later record materially improves the reproduction. Preserve each duplicate's existing body, append a short resolution note naming the canonical friction id and the matching evidence, then use `orbit tool run orbit.friction.update --input '{"id":"<id>","body":"<resolution note>"}'` followed by `orbit tool run orbit.friction.resolve --input '{"id":"<id>"}'`. Re-query the group with `orbit tool run orbit.friction.list --input '{"status":"open","q":"<one distinctive term>","model":"<agent-family>"}'` to confirm only the canonical record remains open. Never treat a 0-hit multi-word `--q` as a clean group.
    3. Verify every surviving open friction against the current tree and current executable behavior. Cite exact files/lines, command output, tests, run ids, or version state. If it no longer reproduces, preserve the body, append the checked evidence and resolution reason, and resolve it with `orbit tool run orbit.friction.resolve --input '{"id":"<id>"}'`. If it is still real, retain it open with the evidence gathered for task filing. Do not guess.
    4. For every verified-real survivor, search existing tasks using the task search/show commands above, including rejected tasks as historical coverage, and inspect the latest rejection rationale for every plausible rejected match. If active or done coverage clearly covers it, do not file a duplicate; record the auditable `<friction-id> -> <task-id>` mapping in the execution summary. If a rejected task has a terminal disposition, append the required resolution note naming that task and decision evidence, then resolve with `orbit tool run orbit.friction.resolve --input '{"id":"<id>"}'`. If its rejection is administrative, keep the friction open, record the rejected-task mapping and next action, and never claim it is fixed; file at most one correctly scoped active replacement only when this workspace owns the issue. If no task covers the survivor, follow the `orbit-task` skill's Create workflow and create exactly one fix task with reproduction evidence and the friction-specific workspace, canonical `context_files`, `friction-curation` tag, and `resolves:<canonical-friction-id>` relation requirements above. Complete the mandatory read-back and repair loop before recording the new `<friction-id> -> <task-id>` mapping. Never resolve a friction merely because its fix task was filed; it remains open until the resolving task reaches `done`.
    5. Repeat the same friction queries and coverage checks before finishing. The repeat pass must produce no further status changes and no duplicate tasks. Record counts and an auditable task-to-friction mapping for every canonical, resolved, verified, covered, created, and still-ambiguous id in this task's persisted `execution_summary`.
  acceptance_criteria:
  - Every open friction was deduplicated against active, done, and rejected task history and evidence-checked against the current tree or behavior; every plausible rejected task's latest rejection rationale was inspected before disposition, and ambiguous records remained open.
  - Every resolved duplicate names its canonical friction id, and every no-longer-reproducing resolution records the evidence and reason through the CLI/store surface.
  - Every terminally rejected covering task has a CLI/store resolution note naming the rejected task and decision evidence before its friction is resolved; administrative rejections leave the friction open, record the rejected-task mapping and next action, and create at most one correctly scoped active replacement.
  - Every verified-real friction is covered by exactly one active or done Orbit task, or by a terminally rejected task with the required resolution evidence; new tasks carry reproduction evidence and exactly one verified `resolves` relation to the canonical friction without prematurely resolving the friction.
  - Every newly filed task is read back and repaired through `orbit.task.update` if its exact `resolves` relation is missing or incorrect before it counts as coverage.
  - Every task proposing to widen a fail-closed guard enumerates the neighboring rejection guarantees that must remain rejected and includes validation evidence for each preserved case.
  - A repeat pass makes no status changes and files no duplicate tasks, and its persisted execution summary contains an auditable task-to-friction mapping; an empty or already-curated corpus succeeds as a no-op.
  task_type: chore
  tags:
  - friction-curation
  - no-diff-expected
  priority: medium
  # The portable system lane is seeded per machine and compatibility-aliased
  # for configs written before that crew existed.
  crew: system
  status: backlog

schemaVersion: 1
name: full-code-review
description: Whole-codebase white-box review at one pinned integration-branch commit, fanned out as one review chore per area
enabled: false
schedule:
  cron: 0 6 1 * *
template:
  title: Coordinate a full codebase review
  description: |-
    Coordinate a whole-codebase white-box review of this workspace at one pinned
    commit of its integration branch. You do not review code yourself: you pin
    the commit, partition the tree into review areas, and file one area-review
    task per area. The durable output is those filed tasks; the execution summary
    is the audit trail. Narrative-only output does not count as delivery.

    ## Rules and command surfaces

    - Use the registered Orbit tool surface. List area reviews already in flight with
      `orbit tool run orbit.task.list --input '{"status":["backlog","in-progress","proposed","blocked","review"],"type":"chore","tag":["full-code-review","no-diff-expected"],"model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
      File an area review with
      `orbit tool run orbit.task.add --input '{"title":"<title>","description":"<markdown>","acceptance_criteria":["<observable outcome>"],"complexity":"<medium|hard>","type":"chore","tags":["full-code-review","no-diff-expected"],"context_files":["dir:<area directory>"],"required_tools":["orbit.search","orbit.task.add"],"relations":[{"type":"spawned_from","target":"<this task ID>"}],"priority":"medium","workspace":"<current workspace path>","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
      Do not use direct lifecycle CLI subcommands; they skip agent provenance.
    - Area tasks carry exactly the tags `full-code-review` and `no-diff-expected`.
      Never tag one `code-review`: completed `code-review` chores are the
      incremental review sweep's cursor records, and an area review there would
      be mistaken for a sweep.
    - Area tasks have complexity `hard` at most, never `xhard`, and no `crew`,
      so each is routed by automatic selection.
    - If area reviews from an earlier full review are still open, do not file a
      second set. Record their IDs in the execution summary and finish.

    ## Pin the commit

    Fetch the workspace's integration branch and record the full 40-character
    SHA of its tip. Every area task names this SHA; reviewers read the tree as it
    stands there, so later merges cannot shift an area under them.

    ## Partition the tree

    Measure tracked lines per directory at the pinned SHA, for example with
    `git archive <sha> -- <directory> | tar -xO | wc -l`. Group directories
    into review areas of roughly 90,000 lines or fewer, following package, crate
    and module boundaries: never split one module across areas, and split an
    oversized package along its top-level modules. Group small, closely related
    directories into one area. Every tracked source directory belongs to
    exactly one area. Vendored, generated and lockfile-only content may be
    excluded; name each exclusion.

    ## File one area review per area

    Title each task `Full review: <area name> @ <short SHA>`. Its description
    carries the brief below, with the pinned SHA and the area's directories
    filled in. Set `context_files` to the area's `dir:` selectors. Use `hard`
    for areas holding concurrency, persistence, security boundaries or process
    control, and `medium` otherwise.

    Area brief:

    > Review `<directories>` in full as it stands at commit `<full SHA>` on
    > `<integration branch>`. Read the whole area, not a diff; read from that
    > commit (`git show <sha>:<path>`) if the checkout has moved.
    >
    > Look for:
    > - correctness: logic errors, wrong edge cases, broken invariants between
    >   callers and callees;
    > - error handling: swallowed or mislabelled errors, panics reachable from
    >   input, partial writes left behind on failure;
    > - concurrency: races, lock ordering, locks held across awaits, unbounded
    >   or leaked tasks;
    > - security boundaries: path traversal, injection, trust of unvalidated
    >   input, secrets in logs or output;
    > - resource bounds: unbounded buffers, queues, retries, recursion or file
    >   growth;
    > - conformance to the repository's documented standards: its agent guide,
    >   contributing guide, standards documents and lint configuration;
    > - tests that do not test what they claim: assertions that cannot fail,
    >   fixtures that bypass the code under test, names that promise behavior
    >   the body never exercises.
    >
    > Verify every candidate against the code at the pinned SHA; a line that
    > looks wrong but is guarded elsewhere is not a finding. Before filing,
    > search for existing coverage with
    > `orbit tool run orbit.search --input '{"query":"<distinctive symptom, symbol, or file terms>","kind":"task","all":true,"model":"<agent-family>"}'`
    > and skip anything an open `code-review` task already tracks. File each
    > confirmed finding as its own task with
    > `orbit tool run orbit.task.add --input '{"title":"<title>","description":"<markdown>","acceptance_criteria":["<observable outcome>"],"complexity":"medium","tags":["code-review","full-code-review"],"priority":"<low|medium|high|critical>","type":"bug","workspace":"<current workspace path>","model":"<agent-family>"}'`,
    > citing `file:line` evidence at the pinned SHA. Skip nitpicks. An area with
    > no confirmed findings is a successful no-op; do not invent work. Record
    > the SHA, what was read, and each filed task ID in the execution summary.

    Give each area task these acceptance criteria: the whole area was read at
    the pinned SHA; every filed finding is verified, non-duplicate, a `bug`
    tagged `code-review` and `full-code-review` with `file:line` evidence at
    that SHA; a clean area succeeds as a no-op.

    ## Finish

    Finish once every area task is filed. Record in the execution summary the
    integration branch and pinned SHA, the area table (area name, directories,
    measured line count, complexity) with any exclusions, and each area's task
    ID.
  acceptance_criteria:
  - One integration-branch commit was pinned by full SHA and every area task names it.
  - The tracked tree is partitioned into areas of roughly 90,000 lines or fewer along package and module boundaries, with every exclusion named.
  - Each area has exactly one filed `chore` tagged `full-code-review` and `no-diff-expected` (never `code-review`), complexity `hard` at most, no crew, `context_files` set to the area's directories, and a `spawned_from` relation to this task.
  - The execution summary records the pinned SHA, the area table and every area task ID.
  task_type: chore
  tags:
  - full-code-review
  - no-diff-expected
  required_tools:
  - orbit.task.add
  - orbit.task.list
  priority: medium
  complexity: medium
  # The portable system lane is seeded per machine and compatibility-aliased
  # for configs written before that crew existed.
  crew: system
  status: backlog

schedule:

template:

      Do not use direct lifecycle CLI subcommands; they skip agent provenance.
    - Area tasks carry exactly the tags `full-code-review` and `no-diff-expected`.
      Never tag one `code-review`: completed `code-review` chores are the
      incremental review sweep's cursor records, and an area review there would
      be mistaken for a sweep.
    - Area tasks have complexity `hard` at most, never `xhard`, and no `crew`,
      so each is routed by automatic selection.
    - If area reviews from an earlier full review are still open, do not file a
      second set. Record their IDs in the execution summary and finish.

    ## Pin the commit

    Fetch the workspace's integration branch and record the full 40-character
    SHA of its tip. Every area task names this SHA; reviewers read the tree as it
    stands there, so later merges cannot shift an area under them.

    ## Partition the tree

    The area bound is **25,000 tracked text lines**, a maximum, not a target
    that may be exceeded. Inventory tracked files with `git ls-tree -r -z
    <sha>` and count each text blob at that SHA (`git show <sha>:<path>`),
    including an unterminated final line. Do not measure the moving checkout
    or count a concatenated archive containing binary files. Include source,
    tests, documentation and authored assets, including files at the root.
    Vendored, generated, binary and lockfile-only content may be excluded;
    record every excluded path and its reason.

    Start with package/crate directories. Recursively split every candidate
    above 25,000 lines into disjoint child directories, keeping files directly
    in the parent as separate candidates. If a leaf directory is still too
    large, split it into disjoint file sets. Prefer module boundaries where
    they fit the bound; the bound takes precedence. Group small, closely
    related candidates only when their combined count stays within the bound.
    Every included file must belong to exactly one area. Use `dir:` selectors
    for whole directories and `file:` selectors for direct files or file sets;
    never select an entire parent alongside its children in different areas.
    If a single included file exceeds 25,000 lines and this rule cannot produce
    bounded areas, report `review_incomplete` with that uncovered path and
    count; do not file an oversized chore or silently exclude the file.

    Before filing, verify all area counts against the bound and reconcile the
    inventories for gaps and duplicates. Write `.orbit/tmp/review-areas.json`
    with `schema_version: 1`, `pinned_sha`, `area_line_bound: 25000`, the areas
    (name, selectors, file paths and per-file counts, total line count), and
    exclusions (path and reason). Attach it to this coordinator task with
    `orbit tool run orbit.task.artifact.put --input '{"id":"<this task ID>","source_path":".orbit/tmp/review-areas.json","path":"review-areas.json","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.

    ## File one area review per area

    Title each task `Full review: <area name> @ <short SHA>`. Its description
    carries the brief below, with the pinned SHA, area's selectors, measured
    line count and complete file inventory filled in. Set `context_files` to
    those `dir:` / `file:` selectors. Use `hard`
    for areas holding concurrency, persistence, security boundaries or process
    control, and `medium` otherwise.

    Area brief:

    > Review `<area selectors>` in full as it stands at commit `<full SHA>` on
    > `<integration branch>`. This area has `<measured line count>` tracked
    > text lines (maximum 25,000); its complete file inventory and per-file
    > counts are `<inventory>`. Read the whole area, not a diff; read from that
    > commit (`git show <sha>:<path>`) if the checkout has moved.
    >
    > Before reading, list this area's task artifacts with
    > `orbit tool run orbit.task.show --input '{"id":"<this area task ID>","field":"artifacts","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
    > If `read-progress.json` exists, retrieve it with
    > `orbit tool run orbit.task.artifact.get --input '{"id":"<this area task ID>","path":"read-progress.json","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
    > A resumed or re-crewed run must continue from that artifact, preserving
    > completed partitions and findings already filed, instead of starting
    > over. Verify its pinned SHA, area selectors and complete file/range
    > inventory match this task. A present but unreadable or mismatched artifact
    > is `review_incomplete`; do not overwrite it or pretend this is a new run.
    >
    > On the first run, divide the inventory into stable named read partitions
    > of **at most 10,000 lines** each. Prefer directory/module boundaries;
    > split files larger than a partition into explicit inclusive line ranges.
    > Cover every included line exactly once, with no gaps or overlaps, and
    > include empty files in the inventory. Read every partition in full.
    > Use parallel read passes or subagents when the crew and execution rules
    > support them; otherwise read partitions sequentially. The reviewer remains
    > responsible for reconciling every partition and checking calls and
    > invariants across their boundaries. A search, summary, sampled read or
    > truncated tool response does not count as a full read; continue in chunks
    > until all lines in the partition have been examined.
    >
    > Write `.orbit/tmp/read-progress.json` with `schema_version: 1`,
    > `pinned_sha`, `area_selectors`, `area_line_count`,
    > `partition_line_bound: 10000`, and `partitions`. Each partition records
    > its stable ID, files / inclusive line ranges, line count, status
    > (`pending`, `in_progress`, or `complete`), the ranges actually read,
    > confirmed findings with filed task IDs, and remaining checks across
    > partition boundaries. Attach the initial inventory before reading and
    > update it after each read chunk, completed partition and filed finding
    > with
    > `orbit tool run orbit.task.artifact.put --input '{"id":"<this area task ID>","source_path":".orbit/tmp/read-progress.json","path":"read-progress.json","model":"<agent-family>"}'`.
    > Parallel readers return progress to one owner who merges and attaches it;
    > they must not overwrite the shared artifact independently. On resume,
    > keep completed partitions, finish only unread ranges and unresolved
    > checks, and reconcile the artifact before claiming full coverage.
    >
    > Look for:
    > - correctness: logic errors, wrong edge cases, broken invariants between
    >   callers and callees;
    > - error handling: swallowed or mislabelled errors, panics reachable from
    >   input, partial writes left behind on failure;
    > - concurrency: races, lock ordering, locks held across awaits, unbounded
    >   or leaked tasks;
    > - security boundaries: path traversal, injection, trust of unvalidated
    >   input, secrets in logs or output;
    > - resource bounds: unbounded buffers, queues, retries, recursion or file
    >   growth;
    > - conformance to the repository's documented standards: its agent guide,
    >   contributing guide, standards documents and lint configuration;
    > - tests that do not test what they claim: assertions that cannot fail,
    >   fixtures that bypass the code under test, names that promise behavior
    >   the body never exercises.
    >
    > Verify every candidate against the code at the pinned SHA; a line that
    > looks wrong but is guarded elsewhere is not a finding. Before filing,
    > search for existing coverage with
    > `orbit tool run orbit.search --input '{"query":"<distinctive symptom, symbol, or file terms>","kind":"task","all":true,"model":"<agent-family>"}'`
    > and skip anything an open `code-review` task already tracks. File each
    > confirmed finding as its own task with
    > `orbit tool run orbit.task.add --input '{"title":"<title>","description":"<markdown>","acceptance_criteria":["<observable outcome>"],"complexity":"medium","tags":["code-review","full-code-review"],"context_files":["file:<evidence source path>","file:<matching test path>"],"priority":"<low|medium|high|critical>","type":"bug","workspace":"<current workspace path>","model":"<agent-family>"}'`,
    > citing `file:line` evidence at the pinned SHA. Derive canonical `file:`
    > selectors from every evidenced source path, removing the line suffix,
    > and add the matching regression-test location. Use existing paths where
    > possible; for a test file that must be created, set
    > `allow_missing_context: true` and identify that intended path. Never file
    > a finding without context selectors. Skip nitpicks.
    >
    > If full reading or a partition bound cannot be met, attach the latest
    > progress and return `result.blocker` with `kind: review_incomplete` and
    > evidence naming each uncovered partition, file / unread line range and
    > unresolved check. Put the same inventory in the task comment (return
    > `comment` in claimed mode) so it remains visible on the blocked task;
    > leave lifecycle transitions to the pipeline. Incomplete reading is never
    > a clean no-op. Only an area with every partition fully read, checks across
    > partitions resolved and no confirmed findings is a successful no-op;
    > follow the workspace's no-diff artifact and validation requirements.
    > Record the SHA, area line count, per-partition coverage, progress artifact
    > and each filed task ID in the execution summary.

    Give each area task these acceptance criteria: the whole area was read at
    the pinned SHA using partitions of at most 10,000 lines, with complete
    per-partition coverage in `read-progress.json` and resumed runs continuing
    from it; every filed finding is verified, non-duplicate, a `bug`
    tagged `code-review` and `full-code-review` with `file:line` evidence at
    that SHA and source/test context selectors; a fully read clean area succeeds
    as a no-op, while incomplete reading reports uncovered partitions in the
    progress artifact and task comment with `review_incomplete`.

    ## Finish

    Finish once every area task is filed. Record in the execution summary the
    integration branch and pinned SHA, the area table (area name, directories,
    measured line count, complexity) with any exclusions, and each area's task
    ID.
  acceptance_criteria:
  - One integration-branch commit was pinned by full SHA and every area task names it.
  - The tracked tree is partitioned into areas of at most 25,000 text lines along directory or file boundaries, with measured inventories in `review-areas.json` and every exclusion named; an unpartitionable oversized file is reported as `review_incomplete`, never filed as an oversized area.

schemaVersion: 1
name: qa-sweep
description: Hands-on validation of recent workspace changes
enabled: false
schedule:
  cron: 50 * * * *
template:
  title: Perform QA validation
  description: |
    Identify recent changes in this workspace and validate them hands-on. Build
    and run the changed software, then exercise the affected CLI, API, and
    feature paths as a user would; do not treat re-running the existing test
    suite as sufficient validation.

    Follow this repository's documented setup and run instructions. When a
    sandbox or other environment constraint makes the usual local state
    unwritable, put scratch checkouts, caches, and other ephemeral state in a
    writable temporary location rather than the machine's real home directory
    or the product's live data root.

    In agent-executor sandboxes and linked job-run worktrees, the repository's
    managed `.git` mount is read-only by design and must not be worked around by
    chmod or host-side gitdir writes. Because `.git` is read-only, commands that
    attempt write access to `.git` fail (such as `git worktree add` or `git checkout --`).
    Instead:
    - To build an arbitrary baseline revision without writing `.git` or creating
      `.git/worktrees/*`, extract an archive to a writable scratch directory:
      `mkdir -p /tmp/base && git archive <sha> | tar -x -C /tmp/base`,
      then build there using a dedicated build cache/target directory.
    - To revert a modified tracked file when `git checkout -- <path>` fails
      because it cannot acquire `index.lock`, restore it from the commit tree:
      `git show HEAD:<path> > <path>`.
    - Read-only inspection commands such as `git status --short` succeed with
      `GIT_OPTIONAL_LOCKS=0`.

    Before reporting anything, search the workspace's configured task or issue surface
    for open work covering the same problem. For each real issue that is not already
    filed, create a durable record on that surface. Give it severity-appropriate
    priority and put the relevant commits, observed evidence, and exact
    reproduction steps in its description. Skip duplicates.

    A non-duplicate failing test that blocks the repository's
    standard validation command must be filed as a durable issue even when
    the failure is sandbox-specific, platform-specific, or otherwise
    environment-specific, including test-harness or portability defects.
    Do not leave such a breaking test in narrative-only output. Distinguish
    clearly between validation impact (the prescribed suite cannot complete)
    and production impact (whether the failure demonstrates a production
    defect). Include the failing command, the exact error, relevant
    environment evidence, and a scope assessment.

    Your narrative output is advisory; the issues you file are the durable
    side-effect channel.
  acceptance_criteria:
  - Recent changes were exercised through their real user-facing paths.
  - Real, non-duplicate issues were filed on the workspace's configured task or issue surface with evidence and reproduction steps.
  - Non-duplicate failing tests that block the prescribed validation command were filed as durable issues, with validation impact distinguished from production impact.
  task_type: chore
  tags:
  - qa-sweep
  - no-diff-expected
  priority: medium

  # for configs written before that crew existed.
  crew: system
